items.title: Baseline severity and early tacrolimus trough are associated with time to minimal manifestations in steroid-free tacrolimus monotherapy for AChR antibody-positive myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: T Uchi, S Konno
items.abstract: Tacrolimus is used as an immunosuppressive treatment for myasthenia gravis (MG), and monotherapy without corticosteroids may be feasible in selected patients. Still, what determines how quickly patients reach minimal manifestations (MM) under this approach has not been well characterized. To examine the time course to MM achievement and to investigate whether baseline disease severity and early tacrolimus trough concentration are associated with the time to MM achievement in acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive MG. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 30 AChR antibody-positive MG patients who started tacrolimus monotherapy (3mg/day) within 1-3months after onset, without oral corticosteroids or early additional non-oral immunomodulatory treatments. These additional treatments included intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasmapheresis, and molecular targeted therapies. The primary outcome was the time from tacrolimus initiation to first MM achievement. Clinical courses were compared between ocular MG (OMG) and generalized MG (GMG) using the Kaplan-Meier method. A Cox proportional hazards model stratified by baseline phenotype was used for the main analysis. Exploratory quartile-based Kaplan-Meier curves were also generated according to early tacrolimus trough concentration. Overall, 26 of 30 patients (86.7%) achieved MM, and the median time to MM achievement was 8.0months. The time to MM was shorter in OMG than in GMG (log-rank P=0.044). In the phenotype-stratified Cox model, higher early tacrolimus trough concentration was associated with faster MM achievement (hazard ratio [HR] 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.66; P<0.001), whereas higher baseline Myasthenia Gravis Composite (MGC) score was associated with slower MM achievement (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.92; P=0.002). Exploratory quartile-based curves showed a descriptive tendency toward earlier MM achievement in patients with higher early trough concentrations. Early tacrolimus trough concentration and baseline MGC were linked to the time to MM achievement under steroid-free tacrolimus monotherapy in AChR antibody-positive MG. These variables warrant prospective evaluation as early indicators for treatment reassessment.

items.title: Characterization of Patients Living with Generalized Myasthenia Gravis Initiating Rozanolixizumab in the USA.
items.authors: Minjee Park, Angela Ting, Aaksa Nair, Alexandria Harrold, Mohita Kumar
items.abstract: Rozanolixizumab is a neonatal fragment crystallizable receptor blocker approved to treat adults with anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody-positive (Ab+) generalized myasthenia gravis (MG) in the USA. This retrospective, observational cohort study aimed to understand the profile of patients initiating rozanolixizumab treatment in the USA. Adults with MG who enrolled in a patient support program (ONWARD™) and/or had specialty pharmacy data were included. Descriptive analysis of de-identified data (July 2023-February 2025) was conducted to summarize patient, disease and treatment characteristics, rozanolixizumab use at baseline, and rozanolixizumab use patterns during follow-up. This study included 877 patients, of whom 51.5% were female. Mean (standard deviation [SD]) age was 62.2 (16.6) years; median (range) body weight was 87.0 (36-180) kg. Most patients had MG Foundation of America Clinical Class II or III (38.3% and 46.2%, respectively); 73.1% had anti-AChR Ab+ MG; 15.1% had anti-MuSK Ab+ MG. Baseline mean (SD) MG Activities of Daily Living score (n = 695) was 8.4 (3.8). Most patients (98.3%; n = 578/588) were naïve to rozanolixizumab. The mean (SD) follow-up for patients with ≥ 1 additional treatment date (n = 393) was 33.5 (19.1) weeks. Patients with ≥ 1 year of follow-up since rozanolixizumab initiation (n = 100) started a mean 3.7 cycles in year 1, comparable to the mean 4.1 cycles observed in Phase 3 studies. In the USA, rozanolixizumab treatment has been initiated in a broad population of patients with MG, with treatment patterns generally consistent with clinical trials.

items.title: Individualized sequencing of targeted immunotherapies in generalized myasthenia gravis across distinct patient profiles.
items.authors: Vasiliki Zouvelou, Dimitra Tzavella, Eleni Strataki, Aigli G Vakrakou
items.abstract: Targeted immunotherapies have expanded treatment options for acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), but evidence regarding their sequencing and individualized therapeutic pathways remains limited. We describe seven selected adults with AChR-positive gMG managed through individualized targeted-treatment pathways involving administered and, in some cases, planned sequential therapy. Treatment selection was guided by disease severity, corticosteroid-related risks, presence of thymoma, comorbidities, peripheral venous access and the need for rapid clinical improvement and/or sustained disease management. Across the seven cases, FcRn antagonists were used for rapid symptom control, corticosteroid dose reduction and bridging therapy while the appropriate vaccinations required before planned complement inhibition or B-cell depletion therapy were completed. Rituximab was selected as a long-term B-cell-directed immunosuppressive strategy, particularly in recent-onset gMG. Ravulizumab was planned as a long-term, non-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy in thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis and in chronic gMG with symptoms refractory to conventional non-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy and dependent on corticosteroids. These seven cases illustrate how targeted immunotherapies may be used sequentially and individualized according to their onset of action, MG subgroup, treatment goal, required vaccinations and route of administration.

items.title: Blueberry Muffin Sign: A Diagnostic Histochemical Clue in Mitochondrial Myopathy.
items.authors: Abraham Alhatou, Omar M Alhatou, Anwar I Joudeh, Mohammed Alhatou
items.abstract: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO) is a rare manifestation of mitochondrial myopathy, marked by slowly progressive bilateral ptosis and ophthalmoplegia that can mimic other ocular myopathies, often leading to delayed diagnosis. We report a 63-year-old female with a 24-year history of slowly progressive bilateral ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, and proximal muscle weakness. Laboratory investigations, brain and orbital magnetic resonance imaging, and extensive genetic testing were unrevealing, and she did not respond to empirical treatment for presumed myasthenia gravis. Muscle biopsy demonstrated ragged red fibers, increased succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activity, and cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers appearing intensely blue on combined SDH/COX staining, a pattern the authors term the "Blueberry Muffin Sign." Electron microscopy confirmed paracrystalline "parking lot" inclusions, supporting a diagnosis of CPEO due to mitochondrial myopathy. The "Blueberry Muffin Sign" on combined COX-SDH histochemical staining represents a potentially useful diagnostic clue for mitochondrial myopathy that may facilitate earlier recognition of CPEO, particularly when genetic testing is inconclusive; validation in larger, genetically characterized cohorts is needed to establish its diagnostic specificity and reproducibility.

items.title: Pregnancy in Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 3c With Graves' Disease and Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report.
items.authors: Miguel Angel Salazar Perez, Maria Fernanda Borbon Reyna, Karen Vanessa Betancourt Padilla, Martin Alejandro Pamanes de la Fuente, Jesus Jaquez Domínguez
items.abstract: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 3c (APS3c), characterized by autoimmune thyroid disease with another organ-specific autoimmune disorder in the absence of adrenal insufficiency, is an uncommon presentation. Its coexistence with Graves' disease and myasthenia gravis (MG) is rare and poses additional diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when complicated by thyroid storm and pregnancy. We report the ongoing management of a 22-year-old woman with this combination of autoimmune disorders. She was admitted with thyroid storm diagnosed using the Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale and Japan Thyroid Association criteria after a 15-month history of weight loss, heat intolerance, diaphoresis, anxiety, palpitations, unilateral ptosis, and fatigable proximal upper-extremity weakness. Graves' disease and MG were diagnosed based on clinical findings, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin and acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and electrophysiological evidence of a postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder. In the absence of clinical or biochemical evidence of primary adrenal insufficiency, the coexistence of autoimmune thyroid disease and MG supported a diagnosis of APS3c on the Neufeld and Blizzard classification. Despite methimazole (15 mg/day) and pyridostigmine (600 mg/day) therapy, and good adherence to treatment, biochemical hyperthyroidism persisted and progressed to thyroid storm. During outpatient follow-up, an intrauterine pregnancy was confirmed. Methimazole was withheld during the first trimester while the patient remained clinically stable despite persistent biochemical hyperthyroidism, and it was resumed thereafter. At the time of writing, the pregnancy remains ongoing under multidisciplinary care involving endocrinology, neurology, internal medicine, and maternal-fetal medicine, with serial maternal monitoring, planned third-trimester antibody reassessment, targeted fetal ultrasonography, perinatal planning, and neonatal surveillance. This case highlights APS3c as an important diagnostic framework for the coexistence of Graves' disease and MG and illustrates how management must be continually reassessed in the setting of thyroid storm and pregnancy. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes remain pending.
items.zhSummary: 本文报告了一例22岁女性自身免疫多腺体综合征3c型（APS3c）合并Graves病和重症肌无力（MG）以及妊娠管理的病例。患者表现为甲状腺危象，确诊基于临床表现及抗体检测，排除了肾上腺功能不全。尽管接受甲硫咪唑和吡啶斯的明治疗，生化甲亢持续存在。妊娠早期停用甲硫咪唑，妊娠过程在多学科团队下持续监测与管理。作者强调APS3c诊断框架及在甲状腺危象和妊娠中需动态调整治疗方案，母胎结局尚待观察。

items.title: Changes in Demographic and Clinical Characteristics of MuSK Myasthenia Gravis.
items.authors: Silvia Falso, Sofia Marini, Martina Marini, Federico Habetswallner, Amelia Evoli, Raffaele Iorio
items.abstract: Over the last two decades, an increasing number of late- and very-late onset myasthenia gravis cases (VLOMG) with acetylcholine receptor antibodies (AChR-MG) have been reported, whereas demographic studies on muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies MG (MuSK-MG) are lacking. We investigated whether the proportion of patients with MuSK-MG with onset ≥ 50 years has increased and whether these patients show distinct clinical characteristics. We retrospectively enrolled consecutive patients with MuSK-MG onset ≥ 16 years followed between 1980 and 2025 at our tertiary center. Demographic characteristics and maximum disease severity, classified according to Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America classification, were analyzed. Patients were stratified into three age-at-onset subgroups. Overall, 120 patients were included. A significant increase in the median age at MuSK-MG onset was observed, from 36 years (IQR, 23-45.75) in the 1980s to 47 years (IQR, 29-69) in the 2013-2025 period (p = 0.033). Patients with onset ≥ 50 years increased from 2/17 (11.8%) to 19/39 (48.7%) (p = 0.015), including 12 VLOMG cases. Males increased from 23.5% to 35.9%. Maximum MG severity decreased over time, with a remarkable reduction of respiratory crises (p = 0.004), with no significant differences across age-at-onset groups. Demographic changes observed in AChR-MG also occur, though less prominently, in MuSK-MG.
items.zhSummary: 本研究回顾性分析了1980年至2025年间120例MuSK抗体相关重症肌无力（MuSK-MG）患者的资料，旨在评估发病年龄变化及临床特征。结果显示，MuSK-MG发病中位年龄显著升高，从1980年代的36岁增加至2013-2025年的47岁，发病年龄≥50岁的患者比例显著增加，同时男性患者比例有所上升。最大疾病严重度总体下降，尤其呼吸衰竭危机发生率减少。不同发病年龄组间疾病严重度无显著差异。研究表明MuSK-MG在人口学特征上出现类似于AchR-MG的变化，但程度较轻。摘要未提及研究局限性。

items.title: Exploring perceptions, awareness, and healthcare-seeking behaviors related to muscle weakness among Saudi adults: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Ahmed M Ashour, Ali M Alshahrani, Bader A Alhazmi, Aliah Alhayyan, Rawan Alhayyan
items.abstract: Muscle weakness is a common health concern that can significantly affect quality of life. Understanding public awareness, perceptions, and healthcare-seeking behaviors is important for early detection and management. This study aimed to assess awareness, perceptions, and healthcare-seeking behaviors related to muscle weakness among Saudi adults. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,000 adults in Saudi Arabia between August and October 2025. A structured questionnaire assessed knowledge of muscle weakness, perceived causes and symptoms, attitudes toward treatment, and healthcare-seeking behaviors. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to examine associations between demographic factors and awareness-related outcomes. A total of 1,000 participants completed the survey. Only 27.8% reported having heard of muscle weakness as a medical condition. Perceptions of susceptibility and severity as well as consequences showed considerable variability with uncertainty evident across most domains. Attitudes toward seeking medical advice and adopting preventive behaviors were mixed, with many participants expressing uncertainty or low likelihood of action. Although some respondents reported willingness to encourage others to seek care and to make lifestyle changes, a substantial proportion remained hesitant or unsure. Approximately one-third of participants reported personal or indirect experience with muscle weakness with impacts on daily life included increased dependence and frequent healthcare utilization. Statistically significant differences were observed in the distribution of responses across knowledge, perception, attitude, and experience domains (p < 0.05 in selected items). Among Saudi adults, there is substantial variability in perceptions, attitudes, and personal or indirect experience on muscle weakness as a medical condition. There are persistent gaps in health literacy and uncertainty regarding symptom recognition and severity appraisal or appropriate healthcare-seeking behavior. Accordingly, there is a need for targeted public health interventions to improve awareness and promote early recognition of muscle weakness through primary care services and trusted digital platforms.

items.title: Exaggerated thymic involution in late-onset myasthenia gravis: clinical and immunological evidence.
items.authors: Heng Li, Peng-Xi Han, Chang Liu, Jia-Meng Lu, Xiao-Li Li, Bin Liu
items.abstract: The thymus is critical in the pathogenesis of early-onset myasthenia gravis (EOMG), whereas its involvement in late-onset myasthenia gravis (LOMG) remains controversial. Herein, we systematically analyzed thymic computed tomography (CT) images and evaluated thymic output in patients with LOMG. We retrospectively examined the chest CT images and clinical profiles of 59 patients with LOMG, 16 patients with EOMG, and 225 matched controls from our center. These data were acquired at the time of diagnosis and before any immunotherapy. The key CT features, thymic volume, surface area, and density (represented by gray value), were assessed quantitatively and compared between groups. In a separate flow-cytometry cohort, circulating naïve T cells and recent thymic emigrants (RTEs) were analyzed in 20 immunotherapy-naïve LOMG patients and 27 healthy matched controls. Patients with LOMG showed lower thymic gray value and larger thymic volume and surface area compared with controls. Thymic volume was positively correlated with BMI and LOMG patients with diabetes had larger thymus than those without. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis revealed that thymic volume, surface area, and gray value were associated with the risk of LOMG. In the independent flow-cytometry cohort, patients with LOMG also exhibited reduced circulating RTEs, suggesting impaired thymic output. Patients with LOMG showed exaggerated thymic involution and reduced thymic output, supporting thymic involvement in the pathophysiology of LOMG. These findings provide clues for future mechanistic and prospective studies.

items.title: Review Article: mRNA CARs: An Emerging New-Old Idea.
items.authors: Yochai Wolf
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has transformed cancer immunotherapy. Still, conventional viral vectors carry risks of insertional mutagenesis, are costly to manufacture, and can cause persistent on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms offer a nonintegrating, transient alternative that enables rapid, modular expression of CARs and accessory molecules and can be extensively optimized. mRNA CAR T cells can be manufactured in days, and their transient expression allows repeat dosing and mitigates prolonged toxicity. Preclinical studies show that electroporation or lipid nanoparticle delivery can generate potent CAR-engineered immune cells. Beyond oncology, transient mRNA CARs are explored for autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus, lupus nephritis and myasthenia gravis, where short-lived CAR expression can reset autoreactive B-cell compartments while avoiding long-term immunosuppression. Emerging delivery strategies, including targeted lipid nanoparticles that program T cells in vivo, could eliminate the need for ex vivo cell manufacture and extend CAR therapy to fibrosis and regenerative medicine. Collectively, these developments position mRNA-engineered CARs as a flexible, safer and scalable platform that complements or potentially surpasses viral CAR technologies in oncology, autoimmunity and beyond.

items.title: Serum Profiles of Pembrolizumab, Cardiac Troponin T, and Interleukin-6 in a Plasma Exchange-Treated Patient With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Myocarditis.
items.authors: Kazumasa Narita, Sho Suzuki, Koichiro Kuwahara, Takafumi Naito
items.abstract: A 77-year-old female patient with renal cell carcinoma, treated with intravenous pembrolizumab, developed pembrolizumab-related myocarditis accompanied by myasthenia gravis. For myasthenia gravis-related symptoms, intravenous methylprednisolone was administered on days 24-26 and 29-31 after the administration of 200 mg of pembrolizumab, and plasma exchange (PE) therapy was conducted on days 24, 26, 28, and 30. Serum pembrolizumab levels were monitored in conjunction with serum markers of myocarditis and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in the present patient treated with PE. An elevated serum cardiac troponin T (cTnT) level of 0.542 ng/mL was observed 24 days after the first administration, and the serum pembrolizumab level was 15.7 µg/mL. After the first PE session, the serum levels of cTnT and IL-6 on day 25 were 0.406 ng/mL and 27.9 pg/mL, respectively, in conjunction with a decline of the serum pembrolizumab level to 4.83 µg/mL. Although the patient had a decreased serum pembrolizumab level of 3.86 µg/mL on day 29, the serum cTnT and IL-6 levels had increased to 0.843 ng/mL and 40.6 pg/mL, respectively. After the fourth PE session, serum levels of pembrolizumab, cTnT, and IL-6 on day 31 decreased to 3.62 µg/mL, 0.381 ng/mL, and 10.1 pg/mL, respectively. The overall removal rate after 4 sessions of PE was 76.9%, after which myasthenia gravis-related symptoms gradually disappeared. This patient with a serum pembrolizumab level within the previously reported range developed myocarditis accompanied by myasthenia gravis. PE therapy efficiently extracted circulating pembrolizumab and IL-6 in this patient with immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis.

items.title: Concepts and Assessment of Fatigue in Myasthenia Gravis: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Sarah Hoffmann, Nishtha Chandra, Channa Hewamadduma, Lorenzo Maggi, Michael D Weiss, Jos Bloemers
items.abstract: Fatigue is a burdensome symptom for many patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) and severely reduces quality of life. Fatigue in MG is described using multiple, partially overlapping concepts, or domains, that are not uniformly defined. The aims of this scoping review were to identify and summarise fatigue concepts related to MG, to review fatigue assessment scales and to evaluate their clinical interpretability, including fatigue caseness, fatigue severity, and clinically meaningful change thresholds. Searches were conducted to identify clinical and observational studies published between 1 January 1990 and 28 February 2025, on PubMed, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, EudraCT and Cochrane Library, which presented original research in MG and used a quantitative measurement to assess fatigue. Following identification of fatigue concepts and assessment scales, a targeted secondary search was performed to ascertain clinically meaningful change thresholds for each scale. Seventy-six studies were included. Thirteen fatigue concepts including mental, physical and general fatigue were identified and summarised, with several concepts overlapping. Eighteen fatigue scales used in MG research were identified. Only two scales, Quality of Life in Neurological Disorders Short Form Fatigue and MG Symptoms Patient-Reported Outcome Physical Fatigue, had change thresholds validated in MG. This review highlights heterogeneity in fatigue concepts and assessment approaches used in MG. No single fatigue scale fulfils the key clinical requirements (assessment of caseness, fatigue severity, and presence of a validated clinically meaningful change threshold). Clearer conceptual definitions and further validation of fatigue scales in MG may improve clinical interpretability. Fatigue is a burdensome symptom for people living with myasthenia gravis (MG) that can significantly affect daily activities. Patients can experience different types of fatigue. Patients may also mean different things when they talk about their fatigue, which makes it hard to measure. This is true in MG research too. This review aimed to summarise how fatigue in MG is described, and to identify the assessments used to measure fatigue in people with MG. We also evaluated the usefulness of these assessments for clinicians and patients using three criteria. These criteria were the ability of a scale to (1) identify patients with clinically relevant fatigue; (2) measure different levels of fatigue severity; and (3) detect meaningful changes in fatigue over time. We found 13 types of fatigue (“fatigue concepts”) described in MG research, with a lot of overlap in how they were defined. Our review also found 18 assessments used to measure fatigue in people with MG. Each assessment covered different fatigue concepts. No fatigue scale used in MG fulfilled all three criteria for usefulness. Only two of the assessments (Quality of Life in Neurological Disorders Short Form Fatigue and MG Symptoms Patient-Reported Outcome Physical Fatigue) could determine a “meaningful change” in fatigue for people with MG. Our review highlights the variability in how fatigue is assessed in MG. Clearer definitions of fatigue concepts and further investigation of fatigue assessment scales could help people with MG-related fatigue feel understood, and be assessed and treated appropriately.

items.title: Thymoma-associated Anti-α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-iso xazolepropionic Acid Receptor Encephalitis with Polyspecific Autoantibodies: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.authors: Ting-Yi Tseng, Yu-Cheng Chu
items.abstract: Anti-α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) encephalitis is a rare, often paraneoplastic, cause of limbic encephalitis. The concurrent presentation of anti-AMPAR encephalitis alongside multiple autoimmune syndromes and antibodies is exceedingly uncommon. We describe a 62-year-old man with no significant past medical history who presented with a rapidly progressive 4-month history of cognitive decline and gait disturbance. Comprehensive evaluation revealed anti-AMPAR encephalitis, thymoma, subclinical myasthenia gravis, and autoimmune thyroiditis, demonstrating coexistence of multiple autoimmune disorders. Immunological assessment identified a complex polyspecific autoantibody profile, including anti-AMPAR2, anti-Titin, anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase 65, anti-anti-acetylcholine receptor, and anti-thyroid antibodies. Following aggressive immunotherapy and thymectomy, the patient experienced substantial neurological improvement. Anti-AMPAR encephalitis can coexist with multiple autoimmune disorders and diverse autoantibodies. Therefore, thorough antibody screening and tumor evaluation are essential to identify occult etiologies and to guide optimal therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Prognostic factors and treatment outcomes for malignant thymoma: A single-center retrospective analysis.
items.journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics
items.authors: Babak Salimi, Sharareh Seifi, Parsa Rostami, Adnan Khosravi, Amir Hossein Mirzaeian, Maryam Mabani
items.abstract: This retrospective study evaluated the clinicopathological features, treatment patterns, and prognostic factors influencing long-term outcomes in patients with thymoma and thymic carcinoma at our institution. We reviewed the electronic medical records of all patients diagnosed with thymic malignancies between 2005 and 2024 at the National Research Institute of Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases in Tehran, Iran. Demographic data, clinical stage, histopathological classification, treatment modality, and survival outcomes were retrieved from the records. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and prognostic factors were assessed with Cox proportional hazards modeling. A total of 52 patients were identified, including 23 women (44.2%) and 29 men (55.8%), with a median age at diagnosis of 60 years. Myasthenia gravis was present in 9.6% of cases. The estimated 5-year overall survival (OS) for the entire cohort was 53%. Survival differed markedly by histology: patients with thymoma had a 5-year OS of 69%, whereas those with thymic carcinoma had a 5-year OS of 35%. On univariate analysis, histological subtype ( P = 0.03) was significantly associated with OS. Our findings indicate that histological subtype is a key determinant of long-term survival in thymic malignancies, with thymoma demonstrating substantially better outcomes than thymic carcinoma. The results highlight the prognostic value of accurate histopathological classification and emphasize the critical role of surgical resection-particularly as part of a multimodality treatment strategy-in improving survival. Early diagnosis, precise staging, and individualized treatment planning remain essential to optimize outcomes for patients with these rare tumors.

items.title: Comparison between mono-tacrolimus and mono-prednisone in the treatment of ocular myasthenia gravis: a retrospective, observational cohort study.
items.authors: Zhelu Fan, Luyang Ma, Jing Ma, Huiqiu Zhang, Menghan Su, Dan Liu
items.abstract: The use of tacrolimus (TAC) in ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) is generally reserved for cases refractory to prednisone (PRED); however, the advantage of monotherapy with tacrolimus (mono-TAC) over monotherapy with PRED (mono-PRED) remains unknown. The present study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of mono-TAC and mono-PRED in OMG. This single-center, retrospective study analyzed collected data from adult patients with treatment-naive newly diagnosed OMG who received either mono-TAC or mono-PRED. The primary outcome was the time to reach minimum symptom expression (MSE, defined as MG-ADL ≤ 1), with time to MG-ADL score of 0 as an exploratory endpoint. Secondary outcomes included the mean changes in Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) and ocular Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (O-QMG) scores from baseline to months 1, 6, and 12 after treatment, respectively, as well as the monotherapy retention rates at month 12 in the two groups. Safety was assessed based on medical records during the hospitalization to monitor the adverse events. Forty-two patients were enrolled (mono-TAC: n = 27; mono-PRED: n = 15). For the primary outcome, the median time to MSE was 6.0 months (95% CI: 2.523-9.477) for PRED vs. 12.0 months (95% CI: 8.342-15.658) for TAC, with no significant difference between groups (log-rank P = 0.253). The exploratory endpoint of MG-ADL = 0 also showed comparable results between groups (P = 0.928). Secondary outcomes showed no significant differences in the mean changes in MG-ADL and O-QMG scores from baseline to 1, 6, and 12 months post-treatment (all P > 0.05). The monotherapy retention rates were similar (TAC: 81.5% vs. PRED: 73.3%, P = 0.698). Both treatments showed favorable safety profiles. In conclusion, no statistically significant difference was observed in treatment response between tacrolimus and prednisone.

items.title: Comparison of the performance of clinical classification systems for myasthenia gravis relapse after thymoma resection.
items.authors: Zhiheng Yao, Hongmu Li, Zhenyuan Yang, Yu Huang, Leqi Zhong, Zhenyu Zhao
items.abstract: To characterize clinically significant myasthenia gravis (MG) relapse/exacerbation after thymoma resection and compare classification systems for risk stratification. This multicenter retrospective cohort included 257 patients with thymoma-associated MG who underwent extended thymectomy at 3 centers from July 2009 through November 2025. The end point was new MG symptoms after postoperative complete stable remission, pharmacologic remission, or minimal manifestation status plus verifiable MG-related treatment escalation or rescue therapy. Death without MG relapse/exacerbation was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with Aalen-Johansen and compared with Gray tests; predictors were assessed with Fine-Gray models. During median follow-up of 41.6 months, 69 relapse/exacerbation events and 21 competing deaths occurred. Cumulative incidence was 20.4% at 3 years and 29.0% at 5 years; 68% and 90% of events occurred within 3 and 5 years, respectively. Among 52 relapse/exacerbation events in patients who underwent surgery in 2018 or later with retrievable treatment-status data, 28 (53.8%) occurred during ongoing immunosuppression and 24 (46.2%) after withdrawal. The a/b phenotype-based grouping of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America classification (1/A/B) showed the strongest separation (3-year cumulative incidences, 2.5%, 12.3%, and 56.4%; 5-year cumulative incidences, 7.6%, 29.6%, and 56.4% for groups 1, A, and B). Groups A and B were independently associated with relapse/exacerbation (subdistribution hazard ratio, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.18-5.91; and 10.55; 95% CI, 4.55-24.47). Clinically significant MG relapse/exacerbation after thymoma resection clustered in the early postoperative years. The a/b phenotype-based grouping of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America classification (1/A/B) provided the most informative risk stratification.

items.title: Unmasking Weakness: A Case of Pembrolizumab-induced Myasthenia Gravis With Concurrent Myositis.
items.authors: Sandhya Srinivasa, Angelica Chan, Minahil Umer, Alainna Cavin, Ashleigh Mendelowitz Calcote, Vasiliki Patsiogiannis
items.abstract: Immune check point inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized modern oncology by enhancing endogenous antitumor immunity by targeting multiple regulatory pathways. Despite their efficacy in cancer management, ICIs can cause many immune-related adverse events (irAE), including neurologic adverse events (irNAEs) such as myasthenia gravis (MG)-like syndromes or myositis. We describe the case of an 86-year-old patient with renal cell carcinoma newly treated with pembrolizumab who developed generalized weakness, dysphagia, dysphonia, eyelid ptosis, and ophthalmoparesis shortly after receiving his second dose of pembrolizumab. Examination revealed weak palatal elevation, mild symmetric muscle weakness, mild weakness of neck flexion, and a positive ice-pack test. His workup revealed coexistence of ICI-induced MG and myositis. He was started on high dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and pyridostigmine, resulting in clinical improvement. ICI therapy was permanently discontinued. ICI-induced NAEs carry significant morbidity and mortality, requiring early recognition, multidisciplinary management, and aggressive immunosuppressive therapy to improve clinical outcomes.

items.title: The Effect of Medication Beliefs on Medication Adherence in Patients with Myasthenia Gravis: The Mediating Roles of Self-Efficacy and Illness Perception.
items.authors: Chaoying Liu, Wenli Jia, Ping Lu, Simei Ning, Guoyan Qi
items.abstract: This study investigated the association of medication beliefs with medication adherence and examined the mediating roles of self‑efficacy and illness perception among patients with myasthenia gravis (MG). Between January and May 2026, patients with MG from the MG Diagnosis and Treatment Center of Hebei Province were enrolled. All participants completed a set of standardised instruments, comprising a general demographic questionnaire, the Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire (BMQ), Chinese version of the general medication adherence scale (GMAS-C), the Self‑Efficacy for Appropriate Medication Use Scale (SEAMS), and the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (BIPQ). A total of 360 questionnaires were distributed in this study, with 353 valid questionnaires returned. The valid questionnaire recovery rate was 98.05%. The mean medication adherence score among patients with MG was 22.40±7.36, and 187 patients (52.97%) demonstrated poor medication adherence. Significant differences in medication adherence were observed according to medication beliefs, illness perception, self-efficacy, disease recurrence, employment status, marital status, type of medical insurance, and treatment regimen (P < 0.05). Medication adherence was negatively correlated with illness perception ( r = -0.687, P < 0.001) and positively correlated with medication beliefs and self-efficacy ( r = 0.231 and r = 0.687, respectively; both P < 0.001). The mediation analysis showed that medication beliefs had a direct effect on medication adherence (β = 0.029, proportion mediated = 37.66%). Medication beliefs exerted indirect effects on medication adherence through three mediating pathways: through illness perception (β = 0.02, proportion mediated = 25.97%); through self-efficacy (β = 0.018, proportion mediated = 23.38%); and through the sequential pathway of illness perception and then self-efficacy (β = 0.009, proportion mediated = 11.69%). Medication adherence among patients with MG was moderately low. Self-efficacy and illness perception played important mediating roles in the relationship between medication beliefs and medication adherence. Healthcare professionals should pay greater attention to patients' medication beliefs, strengthen their medication-related self-efficacy, and help them develop more positive perceptions of their illness to improve medication adherence.

items.title: CAR-T-cell therapy for autoimmune neurologic diseases.
items.authors: Yunhan Zhao, Yunyu Ding, Congfeng Tang, Zhengrong Wei, Yuqing Fan, Xianhui Hu
items.abstract: Autoimmune neurologic diseases include multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, autoimmune encephalitis, myasthenia gravis, stiff-person syndrome, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, and related syndromes. The contributions of B cells, plasma cells, and autoantibodies differ substantially across these disorders; however, the B-cell lineage represents a therapeutically actionable target in many of them. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, originally developed for hematologic malignancies, offers a potential strategy for deep and potentially durable depletion of pathogenic B-lineage cells and subsequent immune reconstitution. In recent years, CD19, BCMA, dual-target, mRNA CAR-T-cell, and chimeric autoantibody receptor T-cell approaches have generated preliminary clinical or translational evidence, primarily in systemic autoimmune diseases. Clinical evidence in neurologic disorders remains limited and spans myasthenia gravis, NMOSD, MOGAD, multiple sclerosis, autoimmune encephalitis, stiff-person syndrome, and CIDP. This review summarizes the biologic rationale, disease-specific evidence, target selection, safety concerns, and trial-design considerations for CAR-T-cell therapy in autoimmune neurologic diseases. Current evidence supports further investigation of CAR-T cells in selected patients with highly refractory, antibody- or B-cell-driven neuroimmune disorders, but does not establish superiority over existing therapies. However, the field remains dominated by case reports and small early-phase studies, with randomized evidence currently confined to one phase 2b trial in myasthenia gravis. Establishing the risk-benefit profile will require stringent patient selection, disease-specific neurologic monitoring, controlled prospective studies, and long-term follow-up.

items.title: Dual-Axis Pattern of Peripheral Immunity in Myasthenia Gravis Susceptibility: A Prospective Cohort Study and Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
items.authors: Jiang Lei, Hao Huang, Jiaxin Chen, Xin Huang, Huiyu Feng
items.abstract: Background: Previous studies have revealed peripheral immune abnormalities in myasthenia gravis (MG). However, it remains uncertain whether these abnormalities precede the onset of clinical symptoms and affect susceptibility to MG. Methods: A prospective study was performed involving 420,936 UK Biobank participants without MG at baseline. Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to evaluate the association between peripheral immune markers and incident MG. Additionally, a two-sample MR analysis was conducted using 731 immune cell traits as exposures and summary statistics for MG from FinnGen as the outcome to assess potential causal effects on MG risk. Results: The prospective analysis indicated that elevated neutrophil counts and inflammation-related markers were associated with an increased risk of MG, while higher lymphocyte and monocyte counts were associated with a reduced risk. We identified 22 immune cell traits that showed suggestive associations with MG risk. Among these, dendritic cell/plasmacytoid dendritic cell phenotypes and a higher proportion of CD39 + resting CD4 + regulatory T cells were associated with lower MG risk, whereas inflammatory monocyte and HLA-DR + activated natural killer cell phenotypes were associated with increased risk. Notably, the proportion of CD14 - CD16 + monocytes showed the strongest risk effect (OR = 2.231, 95% CI 1.370-3.632). After Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, none of the 22 associations remained significant, and none showed evidence of colocalization with MG (all PP.H4 < 0.8). Conclusions: Peripheral immune alterations were associated with subsequent risk of recorded MG, and exploratory MR analysis suggested a possible dual-axis pattern of pro-inflammatory innate immune activation and impaired immune regulation in MG. These findings require validation in clinically well-characterized MG cohorts.

items.title: Good's syndrome and infections in a large retrospective cohort of thymoma.
items.authors: Wenji Jia, Lei Jin, Xiao Huan, Chong Yan, Jianying Xi, Liewen Pang, Chongbo Zhao, Jie Song, Xianglin Chu, Sushan Luo
items.abstract: Good's syndrome (GS) is an immunodeficiency associated with thymoma characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia. The co-existence of recurrent infections may be associated with quality of life and overall survival. Despite its relevance, the impact of GS on patients with thymoma has rarely been studied in large cohorts. This is a retrospective cohort study of patients with pathologically confirmed thymoma recruited between May 2010 and November 2024. Data on peripheral immune profile, infections, and paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS) were collected and analyzed. Of 1001 patients with thymoma, we ultimately included 158 patients who underwent peripheral immune profiling. The prevalence of GS was 45.6% (72/158), and the infections were reported in 43.69% (69/158). Infection rates were higher in the GS group than in non-GS group (50% versus 32.72%, P = 0.0384). Among the 121 pathogens identified from this cohort, bacteria were the most prevalent (52.07%, 63/121), followed by fungi (34.71%, 42/121) and virus (13.22%, 16/121). Patients with infections had significantly lower overall survival compared with those without infections (P < 0.001). In addition, patients with multiple PNS had poorer survival than those with a single PNS (P < 0.001). No significant difference in overall survival was found between the GS and the non-GS groups. GS and infections are prevalent in patients with thymoma. Infections and multiple PNS were associated with poorer survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and intervention for improving prognosis and long-term survival in patients with thymoma.
